title: B198 — Placement inventory: where every workload runs, and whether it can move
description:
**Closing Gaps prework for B134** (the Strix Halo purchase). Do this before the hardware lands; its rows are the migration plan.

## Why

When the Strix Halo box lands, workloads move (a second k3s node, an inference LXC, a MinIO copy). That needs one answer per workload — where it runs now, what it holds, whether it can move, where it should go — and no such list exists.

* Kubernetes placement is guarded (`applications.yaml` + `scripts/check-onboarding-completeness.sh` require a LikeC4 node).
* **Host-native services are hand-listed and have drifted.** A 2026-09-27 spot check of rogueone found three [STUD.io](<http://STUD.io>) GitHub Actions runners, `mosquitto` and `dcgm-exporter` running with no LikeC4 entry; `rag-embed` was described as a GPU service for two months after the reason for the GPU was gone.
* Nothing reads what rogueone runs: Prometheus scrapes only its Ray worker and `dcgm-exporter`; no `node_systemd_unit_state` metric exists.
* With one k8s node, "which node does this pod need?" has never been asked. With two, pods land wherever they fit unless placement is decided.

## Scope

1. `placement.yaml` (repo root, beside `machine-inventory.yaml`): one row per workload (k8s by Argo app/owner, host systemd services, LXC/VM guests, Docker-native). Fields: `host`, `kind`, `state` (stateless / pvc:local-path / host-path / external), `resources` (cpu/mem/gpu), `movability` (movable / pinned: reason / hardware-bound: reason), `strix_target` (k3s-worker / inference-lxc / stays / tbd), `scope` (lab / [stud.io](<http://stud.io>) / personal).
2. **Host-side signal:** node-exporter with the systemd collector on rogueone (and the Proxmox host), scraped by Prometheus.
3. `scripts/check-placement.sh` + bats. Repo side in `repo-guards` (every Argo app / deployed service and every LikeC4 node component has a row; every row names a known host). Live side as a nightly coverage CronJob (servicemonitor-coverage family): a running pod or enabled systemd service with no row, or a row with nothing running, fails by name.
4. The Strix Halo migration table (rows with `strix_target` other than `stays`) rendered into B134.
5. Docs: `docs/hosts.md` points at the file; runbook section; DoD Pillar 1 sweep gains "placement row".

## Technical context

| Where | What | Role |
| -- | -- | -- |
| repo | `machine-inventory.yaml`, `scripts/machine_inventory.py` (B129) | host-collected inventory pattern (packages, not services) |
| repo | `applications.yaml`, `scripts/check-onboarding-completeness.sh` | existing k8s placement guard |
| repo | `docs/architecture/weyland.likec4` | node → component placement |
| repo | `k8s/monitoring/` | scrape configs + coverage CronJobs |
| rogueone | systemd: `rag-embed`, `ray-worker`, `ollama`, `woodpecker-agent-*`, `actions.runner.*`, `mosquitto`, `snap.dcgm.*` | host-native workloads |
| repo | `docs/dr.md` | state / blast radius per store — `state` must agree |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every Argo-deployed workload, every LikeC4 node component and every enabled non-system systemd service on rogueone has exactly one row; the repo check passes on main and fails by name on a missing row (a bats case each for k8s / LikeC4 / host service).
- [ ] The live check reads rogueone's systemd units through Prometheus and fails naming an enabled service with no row (live drill: a row for a unit that is not running fails; removing a real row fails).
- [ ] The three [STUD.io](<http://STUD.io>) runners, `mosquitto` and `dcgm-exporter` are each decided (`scope` + row), not left out.
- [ ] B134 carries the migration table generated from the rows.
- [ ] Exit 1 = drift, exit 2 = a source could not be read (Prometheus down, no systemd metrics) — never a pass.

## Edge cases & failure modes

* rogueone is a laptop, not always on: its systemd series going absent is "cannot read" for that host (exit 2), not "nothing running".
* System units (sshd, cron, snapd, …) are excluded by an explicit allow-list, not a regex that can swallow a real service.
* CronJob-spawned pods map to their CronJob, not the pod.
* On-demand workloads (vLLM/SGLang benches, parked stores) carry an on-demand `state`, so "nothing running" is not drift for them.

## Out of scope

* Actually moving anything (B134, once the hardware lands).
* Node affinity / scheduling manifests (they follow from the rows, in B134).
* [STUD.io](<http://STUD.io>)'s own placement beyond recording its scope.

Relates B134, B129, B154, B148, docs/dr.md. Detail: [docs/backlog.md](<https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md>)
